title: Embark: end-to-end LLM intake, conversion and runtime-cert pipeline
creator: Diego Morales
description: Goal: implement a single pipeline that takes community weights through staged validation, artifact conversion, variant generation and a runtime certification step that publishes a pinned version + performance profile to the catalog. This ticket owns the glue and orchestration (staging, preflight, canary, publish) and the smoke harness for runtime qualification.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Pipeline accepts a signed weights manifest and produces a canonical artifact bundle (safetensors + metadata) stored in artifacts.redwood/embark/ with deterministic naming
A2: Conversion step supports PyTorch -> Redwood runtime format + deterministic KV-cache layout; artifacts include quantization candidates and conversion logs
A3: Automated smoke-run on a dedicated staging fleet returns latency P50/P95 and token throughput numbers and writes a performance profile to the profile store
A4: Pinning logic publishes a versioned pin (pin:v{semver}) in the catalog and attaches provenance metadata including source manifest, conversion sha, and test run id
A5: Canary rollout: publish to a 1% canary route and have automatic rollback trigger if error rates or latency regress beyond thresholds
A6: End-to-end testable by running `embark-cli onboard --manifest <url>` and seeing a catalog entry within 30 minutes
implementation_plan: 1) Staging intake: extend artifact-gateway to accept signed manifests and store raw blobs in /embark/raw/<manifest-id>
2) Conversion worker: container that runs convert-v2 (supports safetensors, merge-sliced checkpoints), emits normalized artifact + conversion-metadata.json
3) Variants: generate a small set of runtime-friendly variants (fp16, int8-awq, int8-group) and attach quant-profiles
4) Smoke harness: run generation workloads (chat and long-context) against a staging serving pool; collect token-level telemetry and KV cache hit rates
5) Validator: run safety/manifest checks (licenses, file checksums, tokenizer match), and deterministic output checks using a small canonical prompt set
6) Pin & publish: create catalog pin, store performance profile and provenance, kick off canary rollout policy
7) Observability: add dashboard widgets and alerts for canary regressions, and surface conversion failures in the Console
tech_notes: Conversion tool: prefer safetensors output and deterministic file ordering to avoid non-deterministic hashes
Quantization candidates: AWQ int8 and groupwise int8. AWQ preferred for decoder-only models where quant-noise was measured low in benchmark suite
KV cache: conversion must ensure consistent kv-layout and ordering so runtime kernels can reuse existing cache indices; add checksum for kv-shape in metadata
Deterministic validation: include a small 8-prompt goldset (chat and single-turn) stored in test-assets; store outputs and compare token-level diffs with tolerance thresholds
Runtime flags for smoke: --no-batched-autoscale, --kv-cache-mode=strict, run with seq_len=1024 and seq_len=4096 workloads
Profile schema: fields required - model_pin, variant, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, memory_bytes, kv_hit_rate, conversion_sha
risks: Licensing: some community weights have incompatible licenses or missing attribution; must block publish until cleared
Conversion failures: large checkpoint sharding strategies can cause OOM in conversion worker; need autoscaling/spot for conversion job
Profiling flakiness: noisy runtime infra can skew p95; require minimum of 3 runs across separate staging nodes
Provenance tampering: if manifests are unsigned we risk ambiguous origin, require signed manifests or chain-of-trust
QA coverage: edge-case tokenizers (byte-level vs sentencepiece) can produce divergent outputs; include tokenizer validation step
